activities.anchor: The field's central methodological pair comes from linguistics
activities.caption: find the faulty line — a methods briefing
activities.name: wtDimSpot

config.prompt: One line of this briefing on Smart's seven dimensions is wrong — click it:
lines: Ninian Smart's seven dimensions: ritual, narrative and mythic, experiential, social and institutional, ethical and legal, doctrinal, and material.
The dimensions do not define religion — they give the comparativist a checklist of where to look.
They make visible why traditions differ: Buddhism is thin on doctrine about a creator god and thick on practice.
The dimensions define religion once and for all, so any tradition lacking one dimension is not a religion.
config.correction: The dimensions are a checklist of where to look, not a membership test — they do not define religion.
config.why: That is what makes them a comparative scaffold: traditions can be compared dimension by dimension rather than ranked by resemblance to one model.

activities.anchor: Comparisons get traction because traditions answer a shared question set
activities.caption: pair each shared question with its answer space
activities.name: wtQuestionMatch

config.prompt: The question set every tradition answers — pair each question with its answer space:

pairs.right: one God, many gods, an impersonal absolute — or no god at all
sin, ignorance, suffering, disharmony — each diagnosis generates its own prescription
scripture, priesthood, direct experience, or lineage

config.why: The question set is shared; the answers are not — which is why the comparative method compares answers, not keywords.

activities.anchor: The oldest continuous family of traditions on the timeline
activities.caption: file each layer of Hinduism by its stratum
activities.name: wtHinduSort

config.prompt: A family of traditions in layers — file each element:

items.label: hymn collections composed in Sanskrit c. 1500–900 BCE, preserved by exact oral recitation
the inner self (ātman) explored until it meets ultimate reality (Brahman)
karma — the law that actions bear fruit, driving the cycle of rebirth
duty, law and right order, elaborated in the Mahābhārata and Rāmāyaṇa
the Bhagavad Gītā's teaching: one's own duty, done without attachment to results
passionate devotional love toward a personal god, open to those excluded from Sanskrit ritual learning

config.why: Modern Hinduism is the still-evolving sum of the layers — which is why scholars describe it as a family of traditions: devoted monotheists, many-gods worshippers and impersonal-absolute orienters all count.

activities.anchor: Emerging in the same century as Jainism's rigorous non-violence
activities.caption: true or false — the Buddhist framework
activities.name: wtBuddhaJudge

statements.s: Buddhism is non-theistic: the Buddha is a teacher, not a creator god.
statements.why: The tradition's engine is the claim that craving can be trained out — verifiable in one's own experience.

statements.s: Theravada preserves the earliest texts and holds up the arhat ideal.
statements.why: Dominant in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia — liberation through disciplined monastic practice.

statements.s: The bodhisattva attains liberation alone and exits early.
statements.why: The Mahayana bodhisattva vows to delay final nirvana until all beings can cross — compassion made structurally primary.

statements.s: Vajrayana's tantric paths add a third current in Tibet, Bhutan and Mongolia.
statements.why: 'Two vehicles, many cultures' is the honest summary — every culture that received the four truths rewrote the packaging.

activities.caption: order the Abrahamic line and its neighbours
activities.name: wtAbrahamicOrder

config.prompt: The line from stele to Sikhism — order chronologically:
items: Merneptah's stele — the earliest archaeological mention of Israel (c. 1208 BCE)
Jesus of Nazareth executed; his followers' resurrection claim founds a movement (c. 30 CE)
Christianity becomes the Roman empire's official religion (by 380)
Muhammad's revelations begin (c. 610) and the hijra to Medina starts the Islamic calendar (622)
Guru Nanak founds Sikhism in Punjab (1469–1539)
config.why: Covenant, church and tawhid, then the youngest of the five: the langar — a free shared meal for everyone regardless of caste, creed or wealth — is Sikhism's teaching in edible form.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — where Sikh authority sits
activities.name: wtSikhCloze

config.text: The tradition has its own institutions and self-understanding: ten human Gurus, and after them authority vested in the scripture itself — the %%0%% — with the langar's radical equality made %%1%%.
config.hint: The living authority is a scripture; the equality is not merely taught.

activities.caption: pair each argument with its starting point
activities.name: wtArgMatch

config.prompt: The classical arguments — pair each with where it starts:

pairs.right: from existence itself — everything that begins to exist has a cause (Aquinas's five ways; al-Ghazali's kalām)
from order — Paley's watch implies a watchmaker; nature is more mechanism still
from the concept alone — Anselm's 'that than which nothing greater can be conceived'
it is always more likely that witnesses err than that nature's uniformity breaks

config.why: 'Charitably staged' is the methodological rule: argue against the strongest version of the opposing case, and mark the boundary between assessing philosophy and the lived tradition.

activities.anchor: Three currents run beneath the survey
activities.caption: call the span from Vedas to Parliament
activities.name: wtParliamentEst

config.prompt: Roughly how many years separate the Vedas' oldest hymns (c. 1500 BCE) from the 1893 World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago?
config.why: About 3,400 years — from Vedic ritual to Vivekananda's address, the pattern holds: traditions are not fossils of founding moments but ongoing arguments about meaning.
